newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end up after deregulation package.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end up after deregulation package.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended up but off earlier highs on Tuesday on the back of sustained buying in blue chips and active buying in secondaries as market sentiment on Monday's economic deregulation package improved, brokers said.

The Jakarta Composite Index ended 2.83 points, or 0.38 percent higher, at 740.83 points after hitting a record high of 741.54 points earlier. Gainers led losers by 75 to 53, with 69 counters unchanged. Total turnover was about 475 billion rupiah.

Although brokers and analysts said the deregulation package lacked details, they believed the proposed tariff cuts on 1,600 items and curbed loans to the property sector would have a positive effect on the Indonesian economy.
"The sectoral impact of the deregulation package is small, but it will improve sentiment in the Indonesia economy in general," a broker with a local major firm said.
The head broker of a Japanese firm said the opportunity for the index to gain further was high on Wednesday on a possible further buying in blue chip stocks.

Brokers said the deregulation package had helped boost sentiment on few counters plantation company Bakrie Sumatra Plantation and fishery firms Daya Guna and shipping firm Berlian on expectation of higher earnings.
Brokers said active buying in several secondaries was partly due to speculation such as possible stock splits and other corporate actions.
Tyre maker Gajah Tunggal and Gajah Tunggal Petrochem Indonesia of the Gajah Tunggal group made sharp gains on market talk that both firms will split their nominal value of stocks soon, brokers said.
Blue chip telecommunications Telkom, Bank Negara Indonesia, Semen Gresik and Citra Marga Nusaphala Persada were among the target of buyers, brokers said.
